title: Prefill/Decode Priority Simulator and Golden Catalog for CI Perf Gates
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem: Our current CI perf gates rely on isolated microbenchmarks (single model, fixed seq len) and don't cover the interaction between kernel selection, attention optimizations, and the prefill/decode scheduling policies used in production. This yields blind spots: regressions that only surface under mixed prefills + decode workloads or when KV cache hit patterns vary.

Goal: Build a simulation-based harness and a curated golden catalog of representative mixed workloads that exercise kernel-routing decisions, attention implementation variants, and prefill/decode schedulers. The harness should produce deterministic golden baselines (seed-locked runs), surface cost/latency/regression signals, and integrate into CI as perf gates with statistically-sound tests and automated triage links.

Scope:
- A workload generator that composes request mixes (short-chitchat, long-prefill, streaming-decode, embedding queries) with configurable KV cache hit ratios and prompt distributions.
- A priority-simulator that can emulate scheduling policies: latency-first, throughput-first, hybrid TTR (tail-tolerant routing), and burst-handling.
- Kernel selection fuzzing: flip/fuzz kernel selection decisions (fused vs fallback), measure behavior with/without attention optimizations (flash/fused attention, rotary/ALiBi variants).
- Golden catalog: three canonical mixed workloads (Interactive Chatty, Batch Prefill-Heavy, Low-latency Stream) with seed-locked inputs and run manifests stored in S3.
- CI integration: compare CI run to golden baseline using bootstrap CI tests and an adaptive threshold (p95/p99 latency, throughput, token-cost). Failure creates an automated investigation ticket with diffs + closest golden run.
- Telemetry hooks: token-level latency histogram, KV cache hit/miss timeline, kernel routing heatmap, batch-size distribution, and per-request model variant chosen.

Non-goals: full-blown production traffic replay; not implementing new schedulers in prod (this is a measurement/test harness).
acceptance_criteria: Produce reproducible golden baseline runs for 3 workloads with seed-locked manifests stored under s3://redwood-bench/gold/eng-534321/
CI perf gate that fails when p99 latency degrades >7% or throughput drops >5% relative to golden baseline across 3 independent runs (stat test: bootstrap CI, alpha=0.05)
Dashboard with kernel-routing heatmap, KV cache hit ratio series, and side-by-side golden vs CI comparison for p50/p95/p99 and cost/token
Automated report payload (links + minimal triage checklist) created on gate failure and attached to the failing CI job
Integration tests for the workload generator that validate distributional properties (mean seq len, cache-hit target within ±2%)
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Chen: Initial write-up and scope. Marked P1 because gaps have caused two recent customer regressions where prefill-heavy flows saw a hidden 12% tail latency regression.

2026-02-18 - Devon Park: Architecture review notes - prefer seed-locking at the tokenizer level and also snapshot model weights / kernel flags to ensure run determinism. We should avoid real customer PII; use synthetic prompt corpus and a small set of red-team prompts for edge-case coverage.

2026-02-24 - Marisol Vega (PM): Added acceptance criteria for CI gate thresholds. Suggested adding an A/B gate that can auto-promote when 10 consecutive golden-matching runs observed in canary bucket.

2026-03-02 - Rahul Banerjee (Eng reviewer): Prototype results: hybrid scheduler produced a 4.2% throughput improvement for Batch Prefill-Heavy but increased p99 for Stream-Interactive by 6%. Need to tune prefill priority decay constant. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6892

2026-03-08 - Design/Observability (Liam O'Connor): Dashboard mocks uploaded; recommend a kernel-routing heatmap and normalized cost-per-token axis. Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/ENG-534321+-+Golden+Catalog+Design

2026-03-12 - Devon Park: Hooked up CI plugin prototype. First CI gate run detected a regression (p99 +9%) on the Batch Prefill-Heavy workload; created follow-up ENG-535002 to triage kernel selection changes. Links: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/bench/534321/run/7
